parameters.label: ASSUMPTION
parameters.source: ASSUMPTION: Taulukko 4.5 reports months after diagnosis; the report does not define a month in days. Average Gregorian month used.

parameters.label: ASSUMPTION
parameters.source: ASSUMPTION: Referral arrival -> Cancer Registry diagnosis date is NOT published anywhere for Finland (data/TREATMENT_TARGETS.md section 3; data/DATA_GAPS.md). Range brackets THL Ohjaus 21/2016 section 4.1 step targets: imaging report <=1 wk, biopsy <=1 wk, pathology report <=1 wk (sum 21 d) - from one step (7 d) to 5 weeks. This leg dominates the referral-anchored output; the spread IS the finding.

parameters.label: ASSUMPTION
parameters.source: ASSUMPTION: Shape of the unpublished referral->diagnosis interval (lognormal). No source; swept.

parameters.label: ASSUMPTION
parameters.source: ASSUMPTION: Referral->diagnosis is drawn independently of diagnosis->treatment and of treatment type. For patients whose diagnosis date equals the treatment date (Q1 = 0 in 3 areas) the whole work-up actually sits in this leg; not modelled separately.

parameters.label: ASSUMPTION
parameters.source: ASSUMPTION: Year-to-year variation in a county's number of new lung cancer patients. Mean annual volume = Taulukko 11 denominator / 5 (sourced).

parameters.label: ASSUMPTION
parameters.source: ASSUMPTION: No county-level timing data is published; each county uses its collaborative area's calibrated timing and first-event mix. Counties differ only in volume. Taulukko 11 county categories (curative/life-prolonging/symptomatic, 12 months) cannot be mapped to first-treatment modality without inventing a mapping, so they are not used for the mix.

parameters.label: ASSUMPTION
parameters.source: ASSUMPTION: Timing curves (2024 report) and county volumes (2026 report) cover different diagnosis years.

parameters.label: SOURCED
parameters.unit: days from referral arrival to first treatment
parameters.source: THL Ohjaus 21/2016 section 4.1, PDF p.14 (data/TREATMENT_TARGETS.md). Document watermarked 'Vanhentunut' (outdated); no lung-specific limit.

parameters.label: DESIGN
parameters.source: Tasan design choice, recs/top3.md T3 ('Day-28 ... Tasan design choices, not official targets').

parameters.label: ASSUMPTION
parameters.value: treatment cannot move earlier than the alert day
parameters.source: ASSUMPTION: An alert at day 28 cannot speed up patients already treated before it; accelerated patients are floored at day 28.

parameters.label: ASSUMPTION
parameters.value: study effect sizes transfer to a Finnish day-28 alert + navigator
parameters.source: ASSUMPTION: The cited studies (recs/top3.md) evaluated different interventions in other countries (rapid investigation clinic, one-stop clinic, reflex testing). Their day reductions are used only as low/mid/high what-if magnitudes. Navigation evidence is mixed (Battaglia 2016: no effect at 60/180 days), hence the zero-effect scenario.

parameters.label: ASSUMPTION
parameters.source: ASSUMPTION: Olsson 2020 (recs/top3.md) reports that pathway prioritisation can lengthen other waits; it gives no magnitude for this setting. 0-5 days is our labelled what-if range.

parameters.label: DESIGN (zero-effect control)
parameters.source: Battaglia TA et al. 2016 (recs/top3.md): navigation had no effect at 60/180 days; always shown

parameters.label: ASSUMPTION (effect_transfer)
parameters.source: Cheema PK et al. 2017 (recs/top3.md): time to first-line therapy 36 -> 24 days (reflex EGFR/ALK). ASSUMPTION: effect_transfer

parameters.label: ASSUMPTION (effect_transfer)
parameters.source: Hiu Nian Chung J et al. 2025 (recs/top3.md): referral -> decision to treat 20 -> 4 days (one-stop clinic). ASSUMPTION: effect_transfer

parameters.label: ASSUMPTION (effect_transfer)
parameters.source: Ezer N et al. 2017 (recs/top3.md): time to first treatment -24 days (95% CI 12-35), rapid investigation clinic. ASSUMPTION: effect_transfer
